title: A bar scale in miles for R.F. 1 : 50,000
body: A student is asked to construct a graphical scale for a map whose R.F. is 1 : 50,000, but the distances must be read in miles and furlongs. Following convention, the student starts with a line of about 6 inches and works out the ground distance it represents, using 1 mile = 63,360 inches. Since the result is not a round number, the student decides to show 5 miles on the scale and recalculates the length of line needed. The new length is not a whole number of inches, so to divide it into 5 equal primary parts the student draws lines at an angle of about 45 degrees from both ends, marks equal parts on them and joins the marks. The extreme left part is later divided into 8 parts to show furlongs.
